newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 14.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 14.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

DUESSELDORF - Euro RSCG in Duesseldorf plans to double its turnover by the end of 1999, says Chief Executive Gerhard Schoeps. Schoeps says Euro RSCG is in negotiations for an acquisition in a specialised advertising niche. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Ad group Scholz & Friends plans to expand its business in new media and has created two new executive positions in the field. John Eberstein has taken over the "n.a.s.a." (net activities and screen advertising) post and Serge Tzscheetzsch is new chief of consulting, Scholz & Friends says. N.a.s.a. represents clients including Deutsche Bank, Hagenuk and Reemtsma with their multimedia projects. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Bertelsmann AG chief executive Michael Dornemann is quoted as saying he does not expect the European Union to block a plan by Bertelsmann and the Kirch group to become equal partners in pay TV broadcaster Premiere. Dornemann is quoted in an interview with Focus magazine as saying he and Leo Kirch had spoken to European Union Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert about the cooperation plan. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Soccer's governing body FIFA and the Kirch Group of Germany deny press reports that the media giant is in danger of losing broadcasting rights to the 2002 and 2006 World Cups. Several newspapers had reported that Kirch risked losing the television rights by signing a distribution contract with Prisma Sport & Media, a Swiss marketing agency, because FIFA prohibits third-party deals. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - The scramble to win the major summer interview with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Wolfgangsee begins. Private channels Sat1, ProSieben, NTV, and both public broadcasting networks ARD and ZDF have applied for the right to conduct and broadcast the interview. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

STUTTGART - Sports car maker Porsche AG says it is holding talks with a number of companies including Volkswagen AG about cooperating on the development of a new off-road vehicle. A Porsche spokesman says the company has not reached a decision on whether to proceed with the project and whether to do so alone or with a partner. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Steel and machinery group Thyssen AG releases a study showing a high-speed freight rail link through the Alps would be more economical than building the 250-kilometre tunnel now under consideration, the news weekly Focus reports. A magnetic-levitation train for freight would cost half as much and could be built in half the time needed for the Brenner tunnel, concludes Thyssen, a partner in Germany's Transrapid developmental rail project. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - German vehicle production, driven by fresh demand for exports, shows double-digit growth in June but fails to offset slow months at the start of 1997. Six-month output rose a mere three percent, the VDA German vehicle association says. The VDA says domestic production in June totalled 470,300 vehicles, up 16 percent over June 1996, while exports rose 18 percent to 281,700. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - RWE AG, a diversified German energy utility, confirms that a subsidiary has incurred more than 300 million marks ($168.5 million) in operating losses and restructuring costs. An RWE spokesman says Breuer GmbH, which hires out cranes, made an operating loss of 100 million marks in the business year ended June 30 and had set aside more than 200 million marks to finance a restructuring. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Munich Re, the world's largest reinsurer, gives investors a fresh set of good news by reporting a bigger-than-expected rise in earnings per share for its 1996/97 year and proposing a dividend rise. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
HAMBURG - Insurance group Volksfuersorge says it has named Joachim Lemppenau chairman of the board, effective January 1, 1998. He was promoted from the company's advisory board. (Reuter)

WALLDORF - Anja Coates is new director of the sales development department at private television station Sat1 and is responsible for development, acquisitions and the implementation of new advertising strategies. Coates was previously with MTV and most recently with Onyx TV. (Kress)
DUESSELDORF - Hans-Joachim Fuhrmann and Burkhard Schaffeld join the management board of the Association of German Newspaper Publishers (BDZV). (Handelsblatt)
